slots.intent: Read what the user asked for, in their own words, from this conversation. That is what they want built.
slots.ask: Ask with `request_user_input`, this host's own question tool — the one question, the option labels only. Codex offers `request_user_input` per turn, and its own instructions say to use it only when it is listed in the turn's tools; it is there in the interactive Default and Plan modes, never under `codex exec`. When it is not listed, ask in the conversation exactly as `plugins/hosts/opencode.json` does — the options in full, the reason for each, and what each costs later — and wait for a reply that names one option. Pass `decide` exactly the option they picked. For a brief or a merge, ask a yes and a no the same way and call `approve` or `accept` with `confirmed: true` only on an explicit yes — Codex's own prompt tells the model never to use `request_user_input` for a permission request, so a brief or merge yes may fall to the conversation even in Default mode; that is fine, the rule is the same: a yes in the chat is a yes, silence is not. Never answer on their behalf, and never treat a reply you did not get as one.
slots.spawn-guard: **The block does not reach into this session here.** SOBER's Claude Code plugin installs a hook that denies an agent spawn onto a held node. This host gets no such hook, so SOBER can tell you the rule and cannot enforce it — which makes keeping it yours. Never spawn an agent onto a node the board holds, and never route around a decision because nothing stopped you. Say what is held and answer it instead.
